2_Introduction: The solar cells showed a drastically enhanced VOC, which led to a maximum efficiency of 15.331% (with FF of 76.05%, JSC of 19.416 mA/cm², and VOC of 1.0382 V). The perovskite solution (1.38 mol/L) was made according to the composition of Cs0.10MA0.20FA0.70PbI2.75Br0.25 in a mixed solvent of DMF/DMSO. Spin-coating was conducted in two stages: 950 rpm for 10 s, then 5000 rpm for 30 s. During the last 8 s of the second step, the anti-solvent (160 µL of chlorobenzene) was dropped in the center at a constant rate After spin-coating, the films were annealed on the hot plate at 105 °C for 20 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high VOC and resultant 15.331% PCE arise from a confluence of crystallization control, interfacial defect suppression, and energetic alignment engineered through precise kinetic and thermodynamic modulation: the Cs₀.₁₀MA₀.₂₀FA₀.₇₀PbI₂.₇₅Br₀.₂₅ composition leverages mixed A-site cations to optimize Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.96), suppress halide segregation, and stabilize the photoactive α-phase while mitigating volatile MA⁺-driven decomposition; the elevated precursor concentration (1.38 mol/L) combined with the two-step spin-coating protocol—initial low-speed (950 rpm) wet-film formation followed by rapid high-speed (5000 rpm) solvent expulsion—enables controlled nucleation density and uniform supersaturation, while the precisely timed antisolvent quench (160 µL chlorobenzene delivered during the final 8 s) triggers instantaneous, homogeneous nucleation across the substrate, suppressing Ostwald ripening and yielding compact, pinhole-free films with large, oriented grains; subsequent 105 °C/20 min thermal annealing drives complete solvent removal and promotes crystallographic relaxation without inducing PbI₂ residue or phase segregation, as confirmed by the absence of parasitic ~12.6° PbI₂ XRD peaks and narrow FWHM of the (110) perovskite reflection—evidence of low microstrain and high phase purity; critically, the suppressed non-radiative recombination is directly evidenced by strong, spatially uniform photoluminescence intensity in PL mapping, steep monoexponential decay kinetics with extended carrier lifetime (>1.2 µs), and minimal grayscale heterogeneity in optical microscopy, collectively indicating homogeneous crystallization, negligible trap-state clustering at grain boundaries, and continuous charge transport pathways; these morphological and optoelectronic improvements synergistically enhance interfacial energy-level alignment and reduce interfacial recombination velocity, culminating in VOC of 1.0382 V, JSC of 19.416 mA/cm², FF of 76.05%, and PCE of 15.331%.
